explanation: A logarithm undoes an exponential: log_b(x) answers 'b to what power gives x?'. Because they're inverses, their graphs are mirror images across the line y = x — every (x, y) on bˣ becomes (y, x) on log_b. That's why the log grows so slowly: it's the exponential turned on its side.
bullets: log_b(x) is the exponent: b^(log_b x) = x.
bˣ and log_b(x) are reflections across y = x (inverse functions).
The log is only defined for x > 0 and rises ever more slowly.
